Tesseract alone could not settle the last digit: across 3-10x enlargements, 3 resampling methods and 3 thresholds it gave 233 most often, but also 231, 232 and 234. Matched against 400+ clearly printed digits from the same table (method 150/150 correct on held-out digits), the first two digits match 2 and 3 and the last matches 1 best (score 0.88, next 3 at 0.78, 2 lower). Its pixels have the same shape as the 1 in '931' in the same column: one upright stroke with a foot, without the left ends and right bulges a 3 would have. So 231. The row's package cells (26 34 22 1 76 54 8 1 2 = 224) don't add up to the Grand Total either way.
